about: Every fact, step and limit this update says or shows, with the source's own words. Sources: three OpenAI pages and Todd's own ChatGPT Business Hub screens, all read and captured on Nov 12, 2026 (Central) in the browser on his PC during the live chat he started for this lesson (2:46 pm). OpenAI's pages answer our page reader and WebFetch with a 403, so each was read in full as text in his browser and the passages used were captured there; the captures in 04_scene/assets/ are the record a reviewer checks. The lesson has one number: OpenAI's own 1.2 billion weekly users. It names no person and no business but OpenAI, ChatGPT, Persona, Shopify, Google (the send line) and ProofNotFluff (ours). Not said, though the pages say it: Business Agents, product feeds, insights, the blue check, the claim invitation and locked listing cases, dispute of ownership, what can be edited after approval (website, description, category, logo, policies). Not claimed: that Business Hub is missing from anyone else's sidebar (one account was seen); that trades businesses are or are not 'local stores' (the help page's own words, 'local stores and restaurants', are used, and the voice states nothing about trades); anything about ranking beyond OpenAI's own 'doesn't guarantee'. Round 1 (after the viewer and render critic failed render 2): the 'we searched ours' story, the DNS record, Persona's name, the email decision and the sidebar screen are no longer said or shown. Round 2 (after the viewer left render 3 at 24 s and the facts gate found two clippings cut too short): the terms open the video; the plumber and roofer line is gone and 'Not listed? You may not be able to add it yet.' stands in its place; our own domain check screen is no longer shown; nothing new is claimed.

changed.what: OpenAI opened Businesses in ChatGPT and Business Hub in beta

claims.words: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT; dated November 10, 2026

claims.said: Claim yours, and you agree that OpenAI's AI may call you
claims.words: By using Business Hub, you agree OpenAI's AI assistant may make calls to you on behalf of our users.; on his screen: By continuing, you accept OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT Terms.
claims.note: claiming is done in Business Hub, and the terms tie the agreement to using Business Hub; 'may' is kept

claims.said: It's in the terms. The calls are for its users, and you can opt out
claims.words: OpenAI's AI assistant may make calls to you on behalf of our users. You can opt out here.
claims.note: 'for its users' is the terms' 'on behalf of our users'

claims.said: You also agree not to bring certain claims against OpenAI
claims.words: Covenant Not to Sue. You ... covenant and agree not to assert or commence ... any Covered Claim against OpenAI or any of its Affiliates
claims.note: 'certain claims' stands for the terms' defined 'Covered Claim'; never 'you can't sue OpenAI'

claims.said: It's called Business Hub, and it's in beta. Four steps
claims.words: We're introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta ... Through Business Hub, businesses can claim their business
claims.note: 'beta' is said aloud. 'Four steps' is our own count of what the help page and his screens show in order: open Business Hub, search, verify, identity check

claims.said: One, open Business Hub. OpenAI says it's in your sidebar
claims.words: Sign in to ChatGPT, and open Business Hub from the sidebar.

claims.said: or type chatgpt.com slash business hub
claims.words: the address bar on his own screenshot reads chatgpt.com/business-hub (followed by the create flow's own ?create=1&creation_session=1)
claims.note: on screen the address is shown as the address bar itself (asset hub-address, cut after 'business-hub') and written exactly, with its hyphen: chatgpt.com/business-hub. Claude opened the Business Hub page at exactly https://chatgpt.com/business-hub in his signed-in Chrome at 3:06 pm (the browser tool's own log). On his account the sidebar did not show Business Hub; the video says 'or' and claims nothing about other accounts.

claims.words: Search for your business by name.; the box reads 'Search business'

claims.said: By continuing, you accept those terms
claims.words: By continuing, you accept OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT Terms.
claims.note: the line under the search box on his own screen

claims.said: Three, prove it's yours with your business phone or email, or your website
claims.words: Use one of the verification methods offered for your business, such as phone, business email, website domain, or Shopify. Heading: Verify with your business phone.
claims.note: examples, joined by 'or'; Shopify is left out, not denied. His own domain check screen is no longer shown (the viewer read our name on it as a plug)

claims.said: Four, pass an identity check before any change goes live
claims.words: You'll need to complete identity verification with Persona before you can publish changes to your business information; You may need a government-issued ID
claims.note: no plate says an ID is required

claims.said: Here's the catch. OpenAI says local stores and restaurants can only claim a listing that's already there. U.S. only, for now
claims.words: Local stores and restaurants can currently claim only an existing U.S. listing.
claims.note: 'for now' is the page's 'currently'. The catch is stated only for the page's own group, local stores and restaurants; the voice never says 'local businesses' or 'if you're local'

claims.said: Not listed? You may not be able to add it yet
claims.words: If you can't find your business: If you run an eligible online business, you may see an option to add it. Local stores and restaurants can currently claim only an existing U.S. listing.
claims.note: the page offers adding only to an eligible online business, and only as 'may see an option'; 'may not be able to' says no more than that, for any kind of business, and 'yet' is the page's 'currently'. It replaces the round 1 line 'A plumber or a roofer? Search and see.', which the viewer said landed on nothing

claims.said: What you get: you manage your own info in an app one point two billion people use every week
claims.words: a new way to connect with the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week. Through Business Hub, businesses can claim their business, manage their information
claims.note: OpenAI's own figure; nothing is said about being shown to them

claims.said: What you don't: OpenAI says claiming it doesn't guarantee ChatGPT recommends you more
claims.words: It doesn't guarantee increased visibility or give you direct control over ChatGPT's independent recommendations.

claims.said: Save this, and send it to whoever runs your Google listing
claims.note: the send line; it claims nothing about Google

posts: Queued first for the evening slot on Nov 12, 2026 (8:13 pm Central), two days after the announcement; the slug's date is its place in line, not its post day. If it has not posted by Nov 17, re-read the help page and the terms before it does, and drop 'just'.
weeklyUsersNote: OpenAI's own figure in the announcement: 'the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week' (asset announce-beta). Said as 'one point two billion people use it every week'.
